config.notes:
SPEC COMPLIANCE CHUNK CQL-18: CQL — List Operators Part 1. Test these items: Contains(list, element), Distinct(list), Equal (List), Equivalent (List), Except (List), Exists(list), Flatten(list), First(list), In(element, list), Includes(list), Included In (list), IndexOf(list, element), Intersect (List). For DuckDB-backed FHIRPath/CQL surfaces, test both the native/C++ extension path and the Python fallback where both exist, and compare outputs between paths. For SQL-on-FHIR ViewDefinition chunks, test parser validation, SQL generation, DuckDB execution, and official spec fixtures/examples relevant to the chunk.

When the pipeline is fully complete, set workflow to null, set exit_reason, write all handoff files, and return control to the outer spec compliance orchestrator.

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 App B List Operators (define referential transparency); FHIRPath multi-valued navigation
issues.evidence: define CC: Obs.component.code.coding.code (deep 0..* navigation over retrieve define) -> population SQL BinderException 'column patient_id must appear in GROUP BY'; every consumer (Count(CC), First(CC), CC contains x, distinct, includes, intersect) fails. Inline Count(Obs.component.code.coding.code) returns correct per-patient values (P1=2, P2=1). Repro .temp/qa/cql18e3_2026_08_22/followup.py MP cases.
issues.root_cause: _resource_rows_navigation deep chains kept LIST() aggregate in a PATIENT_MULTI_VALUE CTE without GROUP BY patient_id correlation
issues.resolution: stores_patient_list marker + PATIENT_SCALAR stored-list reclassification of deep navigation defines (translator.py, _property.py)

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 App B List Operators: Includes/Except/Intersect/Flatten accept any list-valued expression; operators compose
issues.evidence: ({1,3,5} except {1}) includes 5 -> BinderException 'Table function cannot contain subqueries'; {1,1,3,5} except distinct {1} same; ({1,3,5} intersect {3,5}) includes 5 same; {1,3,5} includes (distinct {5,5}) same; (Flatten({{1,2},{3}})) includes 3 -> COALESCE INTEGER/NULL[] type-mix binder error. Intermediate define workaround works. Repro followup.py Chain* cases.
issues.root_cause: list-producing SQL (set-op macros, flatten) not recognized by includes/included-in dispatch; scalar operands beside list operands not promoted
issues.verified_in: Iteration 1 (fresh master gate 2832/2832; list part1 parity 18/18 incl. explorer regression tests)

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 App B Includes/Included In: singleton overload = contains/in semantics (null elements considered equal); list-list overload null -> null
issues.evidence: {null,1} includes null -> False (spec: true); null included in {1,null,3} -> False (spec: true); {1,3} included in (null as List<Integer>) -> False (spec: null). contains/in null-element cases are correct; only includes/included-in are wrong. Repro followup.py Includes* cases.
issues.root_cause: includes/included-in singleton overload did not reuse contains null-element equality semantics
issues.resolution: singleton overload routed to contains macro; list-list typed-null operand returns SQLNull (expression level) (_operators.py)
issues.verified_in: Iteration 1 (fresh master gate 2832/2832; list part1 parity 18/18 incl. explorer regression tests)

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 App B First: returns first element, equivalent to indexer[0]
issues.evidence: define A_Lit: {10,20,30}; define A2: distinct A_Lit; define A_Alias: First(A2) -> [10,20,30] (whole list) instead of 10. Single-level alias First(A_Lit) and alias-of-First both correct. Repro followup.py Alias2FirstDistinct.
issues.root_cause: alias-of-distinct define lacked stores_list_value so First/Last LIST_EXTRACT pre-translate did not fire
issues.resolution: stores_list_value inferred via _definition_result_is_list_returning for PATIENT_SCALAR List< list-returning defines (translator.py, inference.py)
issues.verified_in: Iteration 1 (fresh master gate 2832/2832; list part1 parity 18/18 incl. explorer regression tests)

issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5 App B List selector: elements must share a common type; ill-typed lists are a translation-time error
issues.evidence: distinct {1, 1.0, 2, 2.0, 'x', null, null} -> DuckDB ConversionException 'Could not convert string x to DECIMAL(11,1)' at execution; expected typed TranslationError. Repro per_def.py HetDistinct.
issues.root_cause: heterogeneous list literals failed at DuckDB execution with ConversionException
issues.resolution: typed TranslationError via _validate_list_selector_common_type at translate time (_lists.py)
